about: Rumours, mistakes and lies on the road (#1580, knowledge slice G; docs/knowledge-model-design.md §7). Written by hand: every entry is a placeholder for the owner to review. `propositions` are the things people make claims about, each with a neutral `label` (what the journal files it under; never the answer) and the facts (by id, from facts.ts) that speak to it; `check`, if any, is how the Warden can see for themself: being in that village. `lies` are what a person says instead of what they know: the topic, the words, how sure they make it sound (`sounds`: saw, told or common), the `motive` the data grounds it in (an organisation they keep secrets for, a friend they cover for, a grudge, a profit, fear or pride), `why` in words (never shown), and the trust at which they stop (`until`). With the `caught-lies` switch (#1660), each lie's `reason` decides what catching it costs, once the Warden has heard otherwise (from someone else, or by going to look) and asks the liar again: `protective` (covering for someone, a friend) or `loyal` (keeping a group's business) and the liar comes clean, tells the truth, and says why in `caught`; `greedy` (lying for gain) and the liar's trust drops, they guard their other secrets more, their friends hear of it, and `caught` is all they say. `rumours` start with someone who saw it (`path[0]`) and pass along `path`, drifting by a seeded rule (claims.ts `driftOf`): the number grows, and the place can move. `truth` is what was really seen; `core` is the words, with {n} and {where} filled in at each hop. With the `rumour-drift` switch (#1589): `{who}` is a name (truth `who`, a person on the road) that can swap for someone of the same People; `leak` names the organisation whose secret it is (it starts with a member and gets out through one who talks for a living); `feature` is the switch a rumour arrives with. `poolLies` (#1662, the `run-rumours` switch) are lies of the same shape that only some runs have: each run picks, by its seed, which (if any) of their liars join the written ones (claims.ts `liesFor`), keeping the road at 3–4 liars of its 17 people. `tellers` are how the road cultures the story engine has no `biasSeed` for (world/peoples.ts has the Reach's) tell a rumour, in the engine's own bias words (storytelling/types.ts `PerceptualBias`).

propositions.label: The Compact
propositions.source: src/artificer/answers.ts › Tobin calls them the Compact

propositions.label: Whether Tobin deals fairly
propositions.source: src/artificer/content/ties.json › She's never once caught me short

lies.text: The Compact? A story big folk tell about goblins, so there's someone to blame when a well turns. I've been a goblin all my life, and nobody has ever asked me to join anything.
lies.why: He's of the Compact, and the Compact keeps its business from outsiders. He'd rather deny it than say "not yet".
lies.caught: You've been listening at the right doors. All right: I'm of the Compact, and the Compact keeps its business to itself. A stranger asks, I deny it. It's nothing against you.
lies.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › The Compact pays better for news than for hides

lies.text: Salt's dear this spring, ask anyone on the mere: the crust came in thin after the ash winter, and the racks are half empty. Whatever the Gate pays for it, I can't go much under that.
lies.why: She sells salt, and a stranger who thinks it's scarce pays more for it. A friend gets the truth, and a friend's price.
lies.caught: Racks are racks. What I charge is my business, and who I tell about my salt is too.
lies.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Salt fish, salt pork, salt everything

lies.text: Orrin at the ford? A woodwright with an anvil, the way he tells it, and that's all he is. I've never known him go near a hold.
lies.why: Orrin left his hold seat and won't say why. She's his friend, and keeps it for him until she knows who's asking.
lies.caught: You've heard, then. Why he left his seat is his to tell, not mine, and I wasn't going to hand it to a stranger. Here's what I'd have told a friend.
lies.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › I left a hold seat for this forge. Nobody here has asked me why.

poolLies.text: The Compact? Goblin talk for whoever's buying the drinks. I sell maps and rope. If some secret band paid for news, I'd have heard their price by now.
poolLies.why: He's of the Compact, and the Compact keeps its business from outsiders. He'd sooner laugh it off than say "not yet".
poolLies.caught: Someone's been talking more than I do. Yes, I'm of the Compact, and we don't tell strangers. You're a little less of one now.
poolLies.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › Arvid's map case is goblin work

poolLies.text: My cousin Arvid says the Compact's a tale to frighten tinkers with, and he'd know. I mend carts. Nobody pays a tinker for news.
poolLies.why: He's of the Compact, like his cousin, and the Compact keeps its business from outsiders.
poolLies.caught: Fine, you've found out. I'm of the Compact, the same as Arvid. A stranger asks, we shrug. It was never about you.

poolLies.text: Orrin at the ford? A woodwright, by all accounts. No hold I know of has his name on its rolls.
poolLies.why: The Dyprike keep their own business: why a hold-trained smith left his seat is the holds' to tell, and she won't hand it to a stranger.
poolLies.caught: You've heard, then. He's hold-trained, and what the holds know of their own stays with the holds. I wasn't going to give a stranger his name.
poolLies.source: src/artificer/villages.ts › I left a hold seat for this forge.

poolLies.text: Salt? Hedda at the mere told me herself the racks came in thin. I've a few cakes in the wagon, and they won't be cheap anywhere north of here.
poolLies.why: She carries salt to sell, and a stranger who thinks it's scarce pays more for it.
poolLies.caught: Hedda says what Hedda says. My salt's my salt, and my price is my price.

poolLies.text: Salt's short all down the road this year; everyone at the mere says so. The caravan carries what there is, and it carries it dear.
poolLies.why: The caravan sells salt along the road, and a stranger who thinks it's short pays the caravan's price.
poolLies.caught: The caravan prices on what the road will bear. That's all I'll say about it.
